name: Rack switch
kid: The switch on top of a tall cupboard of computers (a rack). It passes parcels to the computers in its own cupboard.
nerd: The top-of-rack (ToR) switch is a leaf: an uplink to every spine, and 25–100G down to the few dozen servers in its rack.

2010.kid: The switch in a tall cupboard of computers (a rack). It passes parcels to the computers in its own cupboard. It has two roads up: one open, and one kept closed as a spare.
2010.nerd: The access switch: 48 ports of 1G copper down to the rack’s servers and two 10G uplinks, one to each aggregation switch. It only bridges (layer 2); spanning tree blocks the uplink to the standby switch.
